messages:
Sam (Product): Quick sync: EU enterprise lead wants a clear roadmap and launch checklist for regional tenant commitments. They asked for: data residency proof, <50ms p50 from EU edge, and audit logs. Need to pick an approach for product scope & timeline. Options I sketched: Customer-Isolated, Latency-Aware Affinity, Phased Shielding. Reactions?

Nina (Infra): TL;DR on tradeoffs: Customer-Isolated = single-tenant pools in-region (best isolation/latency). Latency-Aware Affinity = traffic steering + cold fallback to nearest pool (cheaper but more fallbacks). Phased Shielding = dedicated for top customers, lightweight affinity for rest.

Omar (Platform Eng): Can we define measurable gates per approach? E.g., max provisioning lead time, required capacity headroom, and telemetry windows. Also we should estimate infra tickets: routing templates, pool lifecycle, billing tags.

Priya (SRE): Ops requirements: automated health-check-induced failover, canary policy w/step-down on anomalies, and a mitigation plan if noisy tenant appears. For launch we need a playbook with Runbook IDs (link) and automated alerts.

Maya (Security): Security asks from customer: BYOK/KMS attestation, VPC peering options, and audit log retention config (90/365 day buckets). We need legal wording for "data residency" — product can't promise physical hardware ownership but can promise logical controls.

Jess (Account Exec): Customer is okay paying extra for isolation. They want a 3-month pilot w/ SLA. If we offer a clear pilot checklist, I can get them signed.

Sam (Product): I'll propose explicit launch criteria in the RFC. Drafting quick matrix here:

- Customer-Isolated:
  Pros: deterministic p50/p99, clean audit boundaries, simpler regulatory story.
  Cons: higher unit cost, longer onboarding (~6-9 weeks).
  Gates: pool provisioning automation, KMS integration, end-to-end audit export validated, load tests w/target p50<50ms and p99<250ms.

- Latency-Aware Affinity:
  Pros: fastest time-to-onboard, lower cost.
  Cons: weaker isolation, more complex routing.
  Gates: affinity rules & telemetry, fallback contracts (<300ms added on fallback), misroute detection alarms.

- Phased Shielding:
  Pros: commercial flexibility.
  Cons: operational complexity (two codepaths).
  Gates: both sets of gating above plus billing tagging & onboarding checklist.

Omar (Platform Eng): Sample routing pseudo-snippet (for estimates):

```
policy "eu-tenant-policy" {
  when region == "eu" {
    if tenant_label == "isolation" then send -> pool("eu-dedicated")
    else if latency_sensitive then prefer(pool("eu-affinity"))
    else -> pool("global-shared")
  }
  fallback -> pool("global-shared")
}
```

Priya (SRE): Perf gating thresholds I suggest we include in ticket:
- Canary timeframe: 72h with stepwise traffic ramp to 10% -> 50% -> 100% for pilot tenant.
- Error budget during canary: <0.01% customer-facing errors.
- Observability: per-tenant traces, tail-sampling for p99 analysis.

Maya (Security): Also add: verified KMS key rotation policy, audit export to customer-owned bucket, and encryption-at-rest attestations. Those are must-haves pre-launch.

Jess (Account Exec): Timeline ask from customer: pilot within 8 weeks. Can we meet that with Phased Shielding (dedicated for them + affinity for org)? Sales needs an internal one-pager for InfoSec.

Nina (Infra): Rough dev estimates: Customer-Isolated 8-10w (provisioning workflow, capacity planning, ops hooks), Latency-Aware Affinity 3-4w (routing + telemetry), Phased Shielding 6-8w (plus billing/onsite docs). All assume reuse of autoscaler and existing pool APIs.

Sam (Product): Proposed prioritization for Q: 1) Phased Shielding pilot for 1 EU customer (fastest revenue + compliance), 2) invest in affinity telemetry & fallback robustness, 3) generalize isolation for more customers only after pilots. Decision requested by Thurs so legal can prepare pilot contract.

Omar (Platform Eng): Risk: model-variant compatibility when routing across different pools. Need a QA matrix that includes semantic regression checks for fallback model mapping. Recommend a 2-week spike.

Priya (SRE): Action items I think we should track:
- Nina: put cost & capacity estimates into RFC (due Tue)
- Omar: spike on model-variant parity (2w)
- Maya: sample security checklist for pilot (KMS, logs, VPC)
- Jess: confirm pilot customer & get initial InfoSec contacts
- Sam: draft RFC + pilot acceptance criteria (including runbook IDs)

ops-bot: Reminder: please attach RFC to /rfc/ in repo and tag @sre-runbooks.

Sam (Product): Everyone OK with timeline & actions? If no major objections I'll file the RFC and lock the prioritization on Thursday. :white_check_mark:
